route: 3 (published subscale statistics: per-dimension and whole-tool Cronbach alpha)
evidence: Route 3 (published subscale statistics), re-runnable as verify_direkvand_2022_mjsi.R (VERDICT: PASS). The claim tested is that the code prefixes are the paper's five dimensions, which is what makes the .sav variable labels usable for the dimension half of the mapping. Cronbach alpha computed from the live table over the prefix-defined blocks vs the paper's published values (Results): communications 0.733 vs 0.73 (7 items, diff +0.003); whole tool 0.705 vs 0.71 (25 items, diff -0.005). Both reproduce to within 0.005. The other three published alphas do NOT reproduce from the deposited minimal dataset -- professional 0.580 vs 0.85, responsibility 0.161 vs 0.96 (2 items), physical-mental 0.354 vs 0.98 (4 items), social 0.464 vs 0.88 (2 items); a 2-item alpha of 0.96 requires an inter-item r of 0.92 and the live r(R1,R2) is 0.09, so those published figures are not reproducible for ANY assignment of items to those blocks and are treated as paper-side errors, not as evidence against the mapping. Supporting: every item correlates positively with the mean of its own prefix block (communications 0.46-0.79, professional 0.19-0.67, responsibility 0.52/0.91, physical-mental 0.49-0.63, social 0.80/0.82). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the ORDER of items within a dimension. No per-item statistics are published (Table 4 gives factor loadings only, and their within-block descending order does not reproduce -- observed item-block correlations rank C3>c5>C4>c7>C2>C1>c6 against Table 4's descending 0.734..0.476), so nothing distinguishes pr3 from pr4, or p1 from p2. The risk is concrete rather than theoretical: the paper's own S5 Persian questionnaire assigns different items to the professional and physical-mental blocks than its Table 4 does, and under the S5 reading the p-block means are arguably more coherent (p3=3.52 'how stressful', p4=3.74 'want to stay') than under the shipped Table 4 reading (p3=3.52 'how much leisure time', implausibly high for midwives). Table 4 was used because the codes number items within dimension exactly as Table 4 does and the .sav variable labels name the dimensions Table 4 names. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
